records.title: 18F-FGln PET/CT Imaging of Glutamine Uptake Has Potential for Predicting Immunotherapy Response in Hepatocellular Carcinoma.
records.abstract: We investigated whether glutamine (Gln) uptake, imaged by 18F-(2S,4R)-4-fluoroglutamine (18F-FGln) PET/CT, could predict and modulate immunotherapy response in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). Analysis of the Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA)-Liver Hepatocellular Carcinoma (LIHC) dataset revealed that SLC1A5 expression-which encodes a primary Gln uptake channel in HCC cells-was significantly associated with poor prognosis, higher tumor grade, and an immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment. In murine HCC models, tumors with high 18F-FGln uptake exhibited elevated Slc1a5 expression and poor response to anti-PD-1 therapy, whereas low-uptake tumors were more sensitive to immunotherapy. Genetic knockdown of Slc1a5 reduced 18F-FGln uptake, enhanced anti-PD-1 efficacy, increased cytotoxic T lymphocyte infiltration, and decreased regulatory T cell abundance. Transcriptomic and single-cell analyses revealed activation of antitumor immune pathways and reprogramming toward an immune-inflamed phenotype after Slc1a5 suppression. V-9302 decreased tumor Gln uptake, as measured by 18F-FGln PET/CT, and sensitized HCC to PD-1 blockade. In patient-derived organoid-T cell co-culture systems, low-SLC1A5 organoids were susceptible to PD-1 blockade, whereas high-SLC1A5 organoids were resistant, consistent with 18F-FGln PET/CT findings. These results identify Gln uptake as a checkpoint of immune evasion in HCC and support that 18F-FGln PET/CT has the potential to predict and monitor immunotherapy response.

records.title: CA1-Associated Epithelial-State Remodeling in Colon Cancer Cells Exposed to Polystyrene Nanoplastics: Integrated Multi-Omics and In Vitro Analyses.
records.abstract: Polystyrene nanoplastics (PS-NPs) directly encounter the gastrointestinal epithelium after ingestion, yet the epithelial molecular states linking exposure to colon cancer cell behavior remain unclear. We integrated bulk transcriptomics, interpretable machine learning, WGCNA, single-cell and spatial transcriptomics, structural analyses, and in vitro experiments to investigate CA1-associated epithelial responses. Intersecting 2,139 colon cancer differentially expressed genes with 766 styrene-associated genes yielded 159 candidates. Among 45 classification models, LASSO+GBM ranked highest in an exploratory cross-cohort comparison, with an apparent training AUC of 1.000 and comparison-cohort AUCs of 0.999 and 0.925. CA1 had the highest SHAP importance and was located in the WGCNA module most strongly associated with tumor/normal status. Single-cell and organoid analyses showed attenuation of epithelial CA1/CA2 and carbonic anhydrase-bicarbonate-related programs, with concordant spatial trends; TCGA-COAD and Human Protein Atlas data further supported reduced CA1 expression. Low CA1 was associated with reduced metabolic and bicarbonate-related programs and enhanced inflammatory signaling. Docking and 100 ns molecular dynamics showed only weak, dynamic styrene-CA1 contacts. In HCT116 cells, PS-NPs decreased CA1, CA2, and Occludin expression, altered stress-, inflammation-, and apoptosis-related molecules, and increased scratch closure, with generally stronger changes at higher doses and after Tioxolone co-treatment. Collectively, these findings identify a CA1/CA2-low epithelial state associated with PS-NP exposure and suggest that CA1-associated epithelial-state remodeling may be part of the cellular response to PS-NPs.

records.title: A novel preclinical platform to study FGFR2 fusion-driven cholangiocarcinoma☆.
records.abstract: FGFR2 fusions represent the most frequent genetic alteration in intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma (iCCA). However, clinical responses to FGFR inhibitors are suboptimal. A major limitation is that preclinical models do not mimic the immunobiology of human FGFR2-driven iCCA. We developed an autochthonous and immunocompetent FGFR2 fusion-driven mouse model. Using the hydrodynamic tail-vein injection method, we generated a mouse model harboring the FGFR2-PPHLN1 fusion (with or without the V565F resistance mutation) in combination with activated YAP1, and established 2D lines and 3D organoids. We characterized tumors using bulk and single cell RNA-sequencing (n=3), spectral cytometry (n=3-7/group), and performed cross-species analysis using 411 human samples. Tumor-associated neutrophils (TAN) were depleted in vivo using an anti-murine Ly6G antibody. In vitro and in vivo drug treatment with FGFR inhibitors and anti-PD-L1 was performed. FGFR2-driven murine tumors were molecularly and immunologically similar to human iCCA, with selective accumulation of TAN and impaired T cell infiltration. scRNA-seq identified pro-tumorigenic and immunomodulatory TAN subsets while In vivo TAN depletion significantly prolonged survival (log-rank p=0.009) and led to increased CD8+ T cells infiltration (p=0.007). 3D organoids reproduced clinical responses to irreversible FGFR inhibitors, while showing a sustained response to the reversible inhibitor derazantinib in presence of the V565F mutation (IC50=5.190uM). In vivo derazantinib reduced tumor number (unadj. p=0.03) and marginally prolonged survival (unadj. p=0.052) whereas no statistically significant benefit of anti-PD-L1 was detected, either alone or in combination. Our mouse model faithfully recapitulates the immunobiology and therapeutic sensitivities of the human disease. Inter-species and cross-species analyses suggest a critical role of FGFR2 fusions in shaping a cold tumor microenvironment with selective accumulation of TAN in both humans and mice. This study develops a clinically-relevant mouse model of FGFR2-driven iCCA for future translational studies. Accumulation of pro-tumorigenic and immunomodulatory TAN along with poor sensitivity to immune checkpoint inhibitors suggests the need of designing alternative strategies harnessing the unique immunosuppressive nature of these tumors.

records.title: A mechanistic pharmacokinetic-patient-derived organoid (PK-PDO) framework for comparing oxaliplatin HIPEC regimens in peritoneal metastases of colorectal cancer.
records.abstract: The role of oxaliplatin-based hyperthermic intraperitoneal chemotherapy (HIPEC) in colorectal peritoneal metastases remains debated after the PRODIGE 7 trial showed no overall survival benefit for the widely used 30-min high-dose regimen. This has raised interest in whether alternative oxaliplatin schedules, particularly lower-dose and longer-duration regimens, may improve tumor exposure and pharmacodynamic (PD) activity. In this study, we present a mechanistic framework integrating pharmacokinetics with patient-derived organoid (PK-PDO) data to compare two established HIPEC regimens for colorectal peritoneal metastases: 460 mg/m2 over 30 min and 200 mg/m2 over 120 min. A population-based PK model was coupled with a spatiotemporal transport model to simulate oxaliplatin distribution within tumor nodules up to 2 mm. Exposure metrics were integrated with published PDO sensitivity data, including IC50 and Hill coefficients, to evaluate response under dynamic concentration profiles. The long-duration regimen increased tumor-to-plasma ultrafiltrate exposure. However, overall PD efficacy at the population level, quantified using a Hill-type exposure-response model, was not significantly different between regimens. Substantial interpatient variability was predicted, with some tumors favoring one regimen over the other depending on drug sensitivity. Threshold analysis indicated that the 120-min regimen is advantageous only when its IC50 is at least fivefold lower than that of the 30-min regimen. In conclusion, despite differences in PK profiles, both regimens yield comparable overall PD effects. These findings suggest that switching oxaliplatin HIPEC protocols may not consistently improve treatment efficacy and that outcomes depend on the sensitivity of tumor nodules to treatment duration, as reflected by PDOs.

records.title: Microcephaly-causative ASPM mutations disrupt mitotic spindle orientation and timely specification of human outer radial glia cells.
records.abstract: Mutations in the gene abnormal spindle-like, microcephaly-associated (ASPM) are the most common cause of primary microcephaly (MCPH). The mechanisms underlying MCPH have remained unclear, as ASPM disruption leads to species-specific phenotypes. Using human cortical organoids, we observed premature mitotic spindle randomization in ASPM-mutant ventricular cortical progenitors, followed by their early delamination to the basal compartment. Similar delamination following mitotic spindle misorientation could be induced by overexpression of Inscuteable, further linking the two phenotypes. Delaminated progenitors resembled outer radial glial cells (oRGCs), which are selectively amplified in human corticogenesis, but they failed to adopt a bona fide oRGC identity, displaying downregulation of key oRGC genes required for their amplification and maintenance. Our findings link the evolutionarily conserved requirement of ASPM for proper mitotic spindle orientation to the species-specific timing of delamination and proper specification of human oRGC, shedding light on the origins of species-specific vulnerability to ASPM mutations.

records.title: Robust Organoid OCT Segmentation via Multi-View Graph Fusion under Sparse Annotations and Culture Variations.
records.abstract: Optical coherence tomography (OCT), with its high resolution, deep penetration, and non-invasive characteristics, is crucial for three-dimensional (3D) imaging of organoids. However, speckle noise, low contrast, and signal disturbances arising from culture environments and drug addition to the culture medium often blur organoid boundaries and cause background mis-segmentation, significantly reducing segmentation accuracy. Although two-dimensional (2D) segmentation methods are efficient and flexible, they cannot capture inter-slice context, leading to incomplete intra-slice segmentation and inter-slice discontinuities. Conversely, while 3D methods can model inter-slice contexts through inherent 3D receptive field, they face high annotation requirements and computational costs. To overcome these limitations, we propose the Multi-View Inter-Slice Feature Fusion Network (MIFFNet). MIFFNet explicitly constructs inter-slice and inter-spatial graph connections between the target slice and adjacent slices, employing graph convolutions to fuse multi-view contextual information and form a quasi-3D receptive field that integrates both axial and non-axial contexts, thereby enhancing segmentation completeness, inter-slice continuity, and robustness. MIFFNet can be seamlessly integrated into existing 2D segmentation frameworks, enabling multi-slice joint modeling without requiring densely annotated continuous slices. Experimental results demonstrate that MIFFNet-enhanced 2D networks achieve Dice score improvements of over 6%, and reduce background mis-segmentation rates by more than 30% under drug-influenced scenarios. The MIFFNet-enhanced segmentation network consistently outperforms existing 2D, 3D, and inter-slice methods across multi-patient, multi-drug, and multi-cancer datasets, enhancing organoid segmentation accuracy and robustness under challenging imaging conditions and annotation scarcity.

records.title: Artificial Cells and Biomimetic Cells: Intelligent Systems Driving a Paradigm Shift in Drug Discovery and Delivery.
records.abstract: The convergence of synthetic biology, materials science, and artificial intelligence drives a transformative shift in biopharmaceutical research, advancing from passive drug carriers to intelligent, programmable therapeutics. This review evaluates artificial and biomimetic cells as a framework that connects fundamental biological discovery with clinical translation. It examines five key technological pathways: membrane-engineered artificial cells, membraneless organelle (MLO) systems, multicompartmental artificial cells, protocell communication networks, and virtual cells. These platforms enable precise regulation of drug stability, targeting, biosynthesis, and adaptive responsiveness. Recent progress includes microenvironment-triggered release, logic-gated intercellular communication, and virtual cell-assisted high-throughput screening and toxicity prediction. Despite these advances, challenges remain in scalable manufacturing, long-term stability, and regulatory adaptation. The integration of closed-loop learning, interpretable models, and advanced biomanufacturing will be essential to position artificial and biomimetic cell systems at the forefront of next-generation precision medicine.

records.title: The Tenocyte from Atom to Cell: A Critical Multiscale Synthesis Linking Collagen Chemistry, Tissue Mechanics, Cell Mechanobiology and Mathematical Modelling.
records.abstract: The tenocyte builds, maintains, senses and degrades one of the most mechanically demanding extracellular matrices in vertebrates, yet the chemical, physical, biological and mathematical descriptions of this system have developed in largely separate literatures. This review examines the tenocyte-matrix unit as a single causal system spanning eight orders of magnitude in length, organised around five transitions: from collagen chemistry to molecular mechanics; from molecule to fibril and fascicle; from tissue loading to the cellular mechanical stimulus; from stimulus to transcription; and from cellular output back to matrix composition. At each transition, we weigh competing hypotheses, identify where evidence is decisive and where it remains correlative, and state the governing equations. We integrate advances from 2021-2026, including single-cell and spatial transcriptomic atlases of human tendons, the establishment of PIEZO1 as a causal regulator of tendon stiffness, and microstructurally derived constitutive models. We argue that tendon homeostasis is a closed-loop control problem, formalised as a mechanostat with an inverted-U dose-response, and that the recurrent pathologies of tendon-tendinopathy, ageing, diabetic stiffening and fibrotic healing are failures of this loop rather than of any single component. An open-source computational companion (tenocyte-virtual-cell) is introduced, and a prioritised research agenda closes the review.

records.title: Primary-Tumor Transcriptomic Signatures Associated with Circulating Tumor Cells Status in Breast Cancer: From CTC-Negative Remodeling to CTC-Associated Metastatic Programs.
records.abstract: Background/Objectives: Circulating tumor cells (CTCs) play a central role in metastasis by enabling tumor dissemination through the bloodstream. However, the molecular transition from CTC-negative (CTC-) to CTC-positive (CTC+) states and their associated systemic remodeling remain poorly understood. Methods: We performed a transcriptomic comparison between CTC+, CTC-, and healthy individuals using RNA-seq data and a bioinformatics pipeline. Differentially expressed genes (DEGs) were subjected to functional enrichment, protein-protein interaction (PPI) analysis, survival modeling, and drug perturbation prediction to delineate the molecular determinants of CTC emergence and persistence. Results: Primary tumors from CTC+ patients exhibited distinct transcriptomic profiles characterized by the upregulation of genes involved in PI3K-Akt signaling, extracellular matrix organization, and chromatin regulation (e.g., HDAC1, JUN, KLK10), alongside the downregulation of immune activation pathways, including complement, B-cell receptor (BCR), and T-cell receptor (TCR) signaling. Multi-gene survival models derived from upregulated (KLK10, MEOX2, IRS4, RND2) and downregulated (ALDH3A1, PPP2R2B, IGF1R) hub genes significantly stratified patient outcomes (HR = 1.74-2.44, p < 0.01). In contrast, primary tumors from CTC- patients displayed early systemic transcriptional alterations relative to healthy controls, with 1700+ DEGs linked to MAPK/ERK and receptor tyrosine kinase (RTK) signaling pathways, suggesting pre-metastatic immune reprogramming even before CTC detection. Drug repurposing analysis identified Trichostatin A, BX-795, and Alvocidib as candidate compounds capable of reversing the CTC+ transcriptional signature. Conclusions: Rather than supporting a strictly binary view of CTC status, our findings are consistent with a transcriptional continuum of distinct yet partially overlapping primary-tumor transcriptional states associated with CTC- and CTC+ status, highlighting a molecular shift from immune suppression to epigenetic adaptation that facilitates hematogenous dissemination. The identified multi-gene prognostic panels and small-molecule candidates provide a foundation for CTC-targeted therapeutic strategies and early detection biomarkers in breast cancer.

records.title: Single-Cell Whole-Transcriptome Detection Expands the Observable RNA Space for AI Virtual-Cell Models.
records.abstract: Single-cell RNA sequencing has supplied cell atlases and artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled virtual-cell models with scalable, gene-level descriptions of cellular state. Yet prevalent poly(A)-based counting assays capture only part of the RNA landscape. Here, "single-cell whole-transcriptome detection" denotes sequencing-based efforts to detect a broader range of RNA biotypes than conventional poly(A)-based gene counting; no assay detects or quantifies every cellular RNA species without bias. We compare RNA-capture scope, transcript-structure resolution, temporal labeling, spatial context, and additional modalities as distinct measurement dimensions. From a biosensing perspective, analytical sensitivity, transcript coverage, throughput, and assay bias determine which signals are available to computational models. We then examine cell-state representations, regulatory networks, dynamics, perturbation prediction, and foundation models. Total-RNA assays reveal additional non-coding RNAs, long-read methods inform transcript structure, and temporal assays constrain RNA kinetics. Whether these signals improve prediction beyond conventional gene-count inputs requires matched, task-specific model comparisons. We distinguish molecular observability, statistical association, predictive performance, and causal validation, which requires appropriate interventions. We propose benchmarks controlling sequencing depth, cost, model architecture, and held-out samples while testing feature ablations, out-of-distribution performance, uncertainty calibration, and experimental outcomes. Together, high-throughput poly(A)-based profiling and broader RNA measurements provide complementary cellular breadth and regulatory depth.

records.title: Virtual cells: progress and challenges from mechanistic modeling to data-driven integration.
records.abstract: Virtual cells aim to represent cellular states computationally and predict responses to genetic, chemical, environmental, temporal, and spatial conditions. For comparative purposes, this review uses state encoding (E), state transition (T), and observation decoding (D) as a conceptual abstraction spanning explicit mechanistic models, data-driven foundation and perturbation models, multimodal systems, and spatial and multiscale simulation. We examine model boundaries, data foundations, resource disclosure, out-of-distribution evaluation, causal evidence, and experimental validation. Independent benchmarks show that parameter count and training-set size do not automatically yield robust out-of-distribution generalization, while transcriptomic representations alone do not capture the full functional state of a cell. Trustworthy virtual cells will require perturbation-responsive transitions, cross-modal alignment, continuous-time dynamics, mechanistic constraints, calibrated uncertainty, independent experimental validation, and, where appropriate, closed-loop experimental feedback.

records.title: Progress of metabolomics-centric multi-omics research in medicine.
records.abstract: Metabolomics reveals molecular changes at the metabolic level during biological processes. Recent advancements, particularly through integration with other omics and artificial intelligence (AI), are advancing metabolic data analysis and multi-omics interpretation. This review introduces a "metabolomics-centric" paradigm as a conceptual framework for multi-omics integration, positioning metabolic readouts as the functional anchor for interpreting genotype-phenotype relationships. It also chronicles the evolution and medical applications of integration technologies. Our discussion first traces the field's evolution from bulk to single-cell and spatial methodologies, next surveys integration strategies to uncover mechanistic insights, and finally examines how AI-driven multimodal data integration and AI-optimized metabolomics workflows tackle persistent biological and computational challenges. Looking forward, this review identifies the AI virtual cell as a pivotal future direction for metabolomics-based multi-omics integration, calling for increased attention to its development to simulate dynamic molecular phenotypic networks within a multi-omics context.

records.title: LM2KM: feature extraction from pretrained protein and molecular language models combined with quantum mechanics (QM) features for K M predictions.
records.abstract: The Michaelis constant (K M) is a key parameter for characterizing enzyme-substrate interactions and plays an essential role in enzyme kinetics modeling and physiologically based pharmacokinetic (PBPK) applications. However, experimental determination of K M is labor-intensive, and existing computational prediction approaches remain limited in accuracy and scalability. In this study, we systematically evaluated pretrained protein and molecule language models for K M prediction by integrating four protein language models (PLMs) and two molecule language models (MLMs) to encode enzyme sequences and substrate structures, respectively. Principal component analysis (PCA) was applied to reduce feature dimensionality, and a wide range of representation combinations were assessed. Our results indicated that protein representations derived from the last four layers of ProtT5 using approximately 70 features, combined with 20 CLS-based molecular features from MolFormer, provided a well-balanced and efficient representation for K M prediction. In addition, the incorporation of quantum mechanics (QM) descriptors consistently improved prediction performance across all tested configurations, with the model R 2 of 0.537. In summary, this work provides a flexible and extensible framework for large-scale K M prediction, with strong potential to facilitate enzyme pathway identification, drug and lead screening, and sequence-based protein design, supporting broader applications in enzyme kinetics-driven modeling and drug development.

records.title: AI-guided De Novo design of DHPS inhibitors.
records.abstract: Hypusine modification of eIF5A by Deoxyhypusine Synthase (DHPS) is essential for the replication of a broad range of viruses, making DHPS an attractive host-directed therapy (HDT) target for antiviral drug discovery. AI-based drug design methods spanning binding affinity prediction and de novo molecular generation are rapidly proliferating, yet systematic benchmarking of diverse algorithmic paradigms under identical conditions on a shared target, with experimental validation, remains scarce. Here, we present an integrated AI benchmarking pipeline targeting DHPS and evaluate the full process from computational prediction to experimental validation. We compared 13 MM-GBSA score estimation models and 10 de novo molecular generation methods under 5-seed repeated experiments. For the prediction task, we propose an Out-of-Fold stacking ensemble integrating gradient boosting, graph neural networks, and chemical language models, achieving the highest Spearman rank correlation of 0.861 among all compared models. For the generation task, we propose RL-Design, a reinforcement learning-based framework using the ensemble predictor as a scoring oracle. RL-Design achieved the highest hit rate of 92.02% and maintained drug-like physicochemical properties across generated molecules, outperforming all nine competing methods. Moreover, experimental dose-response assays confirmed inhibitory activity in all three predicted-active compounds, with two highly active compounds showing IC50 values of 31.2 and 49.1 µM. Predicted and experimental activity showed complete concordance across all six tested compounds, providing oracle-independent validation of the pipeline. This pipeline provides a reproducible framework for AI-guided, target-specific inhibitor design and demonstrates the feasibility of HDT-focused antiviral drug discovery through systematic AI benchmarking.Scientific contributionThis work proposes two methods for inhibitor discovery against DHPS, a host-directed antiviral target. A predictive model for MM-GBSA binding-score estimation and a generative model that designs candidate hit compounds both ranked first among previous prediction and generation models under identical benchmarking. The predicted activities were experimentally confirmed by dose-response enzymatic assays.

records.title: Simulating Directed Evolution In Silico with an Iterative, Physics-Based Workflow.
records.abstract: Directed evolution consistently delivers engineered enzymes that facilitate diverse biocatalytic transformations. Despite advances in automation and high-throughput workflows, our ability to rapidly engineer novel enzymes is limited by our inability to thoroughly sample the vast protein design space. Generative artificial intelligence (AI) methods have alleviated this challenge to some degree, due to their ability to propose mutations based on learned patterns from complex protein data sets. However, the hidden logic of these AI-based methods can complicate our ability to reveal and exploit fundamental details of these enzymes. To complement these hidden-logic models, we present a structure- and physics-based workflow that mimics directed evolution in silico. This Virtual Protein EngineeR (referred to as ViPER) aims to simulate directed evolution by leveraging computational modeling, molecular dynamics simulations, in silico mutagenesis, and structure-based property evaluation to iteratively engineer an enzyme toward a desired target. In this work, we present a retrospective analysis to demonstrate ViPER's ability to efficiently navigate the complex protein-protein interfaces associated with the oligomerization of a ketoreductase (KRED) enzyme. In addition to successfully predicting >70% of sites that are crucial for toggling the oligomerization of this KRED enzyme (after only five rounds), this dynamics-based methodology identifies a distal mutation that was incorporated during experiment-based directed evolution. This work provides a novel foundation for computationally driven directed evolution efforts, opening the opportunity to simultaneously pursue and evaluate multiple evolutionary routes through a physics-based lens.

records.title: Filling the massive AI drug discovery data gap.
Evaluating generative models for structure-based drug discovery from de novo design to lead optimization.
records.abstract: Advances in protein structure prediction have created opportunities for structure-based drug design, yet translating structural knowledge into actionable small-molecule ligands remains difficult. Existing benchmarks often use simplified datasets and computational surrogates that poorly capture the heterogeneity and constraints of real-world drug discovery. We introduce MolGenBench, a comprehensive benchmark for de novo molecular generation and hit-to-lead optimization built on a large, structurally diverse dataset. Evaluation of 17 leading methods reveals persistent limitations, including weak virtual-screening performance, limited coverage of target-specific bioactive space, frequent high-risk structural motifs, poor target awareness, and reduced generalization to unseen proteins. Although some models improve three-dimensional conformation generation, they still struggle to produce active molecules reliably. MolGenBench provides standardized data, metrics, and analyses that connect structural prediction with practical molecular design and guide the development of more effective structure-based generative models.

records.title: Roads not taken: The mismatch between safety and regulation of plant breeding innovation.
records.abstract: Meeting global food security goals while reducing agriculture's environmental impact requires continued crop improvement and innovation. Advances in transgenesis, cisgenesis, and genome editing now enable increasingly precise genetic modification with risks comparable to those of conventional breeding, yet regulatory frameworks remain focused on the method used rather than the product. We highlight recent examples, including immune receptor transfer, cisgenesis-based disease resistance stacking, photosynthesis engineering, and AI-guided protein design, that illustrate innovations constrained by current regulatory approaches. A decisive shift toward science-based, proportionate, and product-focused regulation is needed so that improved crops are evaluated on the basis of their properties, not how they were made.

records.title: DNA damage response and repair signaling: Emerging biomarkers and therapeutic targets in human cancers.
records.abstract: Maintenance of genomic integrity is essential for proper cellular function and for protecting against malignant transformation. Prolonged exposure to endogenous and exogenous genotoxic environments results in multiple forms of DNA damage, including single-strand breaks, double-strand breaks, oxidative lesions, base mismatches, and replication-associated abnormalities. Cells possess a meticulously regulated DDR network of specialized sensor proteins, checkpoint regulators, signal mediators, and repair pathways to address various damages. Key repair mechanisms, such as BER, NER, MMR, HRR, NHEJ, and Alt-EJ, collectively maintain genomic stability and regulate cellular viability in response to genotoxic stress. Aberrant expression of DDR-associated molecular partners significantly contributes to genomic instability, tumorigenesis, progression, metastasis, and therapy resistance in specific malignancies. Recent advancements in molecular oncology have underscored the translational significance of DDR signaling in cancer diagnosis, prognosis, and targeted therapy. Synthetic lethality methods, particularly PARP inhibition in malignancies that impair HR, have transformed precision oncology. Moreover, recent data indicate significant interactions between DDR mechanisms and various cancer hallmarks, including epigenetic regulation, metabolic reprogramming, immune modulation, adaptation to replication stress, and TME signaling. This review focuses on the diagnostic and translational significance of DDR alterations in human cancers, with particular emphasis on biomarker interpretation and clinical efficacy. Current approaches for HRD and MMR/MSI assessment, including genomic, functional and liquid-biopsy strategies, are considered together with their pre-analytical and analytical limitations. The review further examines how DDR biomarkers inform targeted treatment selection, resistance monitoring, and emerging approaches, while highlighting unresolved challenges in assay validation, tumor heterogeneity, dynamic biomarker evolution, and clinical implementation. PLAIN LANGUAGE SUMMARY: DNA in our cells is constantly being damaged by normal cellular processes and environmental factors such as radiation and harmful chemicals. Cells contain protective systems called the DNA damage response (DDR) and DNA repair pathways that are capable of detecting and repairing this damage. When these systems become defective, DNA modifications can accumulate and contribute to cancer development, progression, and resistance to treatment. This review explains how major DNA repair pathways maintain genomic stability and how alterations in these pathways might generate vulnerabilities that can be used to treat cancer. It also addresses the established and emerging therapies targeting DNA repair vulnerabilities such as PARP, ATR, ATM, CHK1, WEE1, DNA-PK, and POLQ inhibitors. It also discusses why certain tumors do not respond or develop resistance to these therapies and why biomarkers do not always accurately predict treatment effectiveness. The review also covers the interactions between DNA damage and the immune system, such as context-dependent functions of cGAS-STING signaling. Finally, emerging methods such as functional DNA-repair tests, circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA), single-cell and spatial analysis, and multi-omics may improve patient selection and assist in leading more personalized and effective cancer treatment.

records.title: Clinical utility of Circulating Long Non-Coding RNAs in indeterminate thyroid nodules.
records.abstract: Indeterminate cytology results (Bethesda categories III and IV) from fine-needle aspiration (FNA) create challenges in clinical decision-making. This study evaluated the expression and diagnostic utility of selected long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) in cell-free plasma from patients with indeterminate thyroid nodules. Prospective, single-center study. Nine candidate long non-coding RNA were selected from a curated disease database. A total of 126 individuals with solitary thyroid nodules were enrolled. RNA was extracted from plasma, FNA, and tissue samples and expression levels were measured using quantitative real-time PCR. In the discovery cohort, patients with benign and malignant nodules confirmed by histopathology, were used to determine optimal cut-off values through receiver operating characteristic analysis. Spearman correlation analyses were performed to assess concordance between plasma and FNA/tissue expression. In the validation phase, significantly altered markers were applied to indeterminate nodules to assess diagnostic performance. In the discovery cohort, PVT1, MALAT1, and BANCR were significantly upregulated in malignant compared with benign nodules (P < 0.0001). Significant positive correlations were observed between plasma and FNA expression for PVT1 (r = 0.7095), MALAT1 (r = 0.5487), and BANCR (r = 0.6792), and between plasma and tissue expression for PVT1 (r = 0.7673), MALAT1 (r = 0.5284), and BANCR (r = 0.6864) (P < 0.0001). In the Bethesda III/IV validation cohort, only PVT1 retained diagnostic utility, with 76% sensitivity, 87.5% specificity, 85% positive predictive value, and 80% negative predictive value, whereas MALAT1 and BANCR did not demonstrate significant diagnostic performance. Circulating PVT1 expression in plasma may serve as a useful non-invasive biomarker for distinguishing benign from malignant indeterminate thyroid nodules.

records.title: Transformer-Guided Co-Optimization of Mutation Prioritization and Thermodynamic Probe Design for Mutation Detection.
records.abstract: The design of sequence-selective DNA probes has long been limited by a decoupled workflow in which target selection proceeds without considering the physicochemical determinants of probe performance, such as thermodynamic stability and mismatch discrimination. Here, we establish an iterative computational design strategy that unifies mutation prioritization with chemical probe design. A custom transformer model extracts diagnostic attribution scores of mutations from 1,782 samples, generating semantic maps to guide probe placement. Candidate designs undergo in silico thermodynamic screening based on differential binding free energy. Probes failing to satisfy the integrated criteria of thermodynamic discrimination, diagnostic attribution, and population frequency are further evaluated by refining their spatial configuration to co-optimize thermodynamic discriminability and clinical relevance. This iterative process converges on an 8-plex targeted panel. Wet laboratory validation confirms 0.03% variant allele frequency detection with low assay cost and short turnaround time. Clinical testing on 375 samples achieves AUROC values of 0.96 for tissue and 0.90 for plasma. This work provides a potential chemical framework for nucleic acid probe design that could be explored in other molecular diagnostic systems.

records.title: Feasibility of Shallow Whole-Genome Sequencing-Based Circulating Tumour DNA Analysis in Canine Multicentric Lymphoma: A Pilot Study.
records.abstract: Lymphoma is a common canine malignancy with high morbidity and variable prognosis. Circulating tumour DNA (ctDNA) has emerged as a minimally invasive biomarker for tumour burden, treatment response and prognosis in human lymphoma. However, the feasibility of applying shallow whole-genome sequencing (sWGS)-based ctDNA analysis to canine lymphoma remains unclear. In this pilot study, plasma cell-free DNA (cfDNA) was quantitatively assessed and additional genomic features were evaluated using sWGS in dogs with multicentric lymphoma. cfDNA concentration was significantly higher in dogs with lymphoma (n = 13) compared with healthy controls (n = 24) (median 3.18 vs. 0.25 ng/mL; Mann-Whitney U test, p = 0.004). However, total cfDNA concentration was not significantly associated with time to progression (TTP) (p = 0.055). Tumour fraction (TF), a surrogate for ctDNA, showed preliminary association with clinical outcome, with a shorter median TTP in the high-TF group than in the low-TF group (77 vs. 302 days; p = 0.006). Genomic analysis further revealed copy number aberrations (CNAs); notably, gains on chromosome 13 containing the MYC locus were identified in three dogs, all of which belonged to the high-TF group. Dogs with lymphoma also displayed distinct cfDNA fragmentation profiles, characterized by an enrichment of shorter fragments within the analysed size range and a shift in the highest mean-profile peak compared with healthy controls. These findings demonstrate the feasibility of sWGS-based cfDNA analysis in canine lymphoma and suggest that TF may provide clinically relevant information beyond total cfDNA concentration. Validation in a substantially larger, independent cohort is warranted.

records.title: KRAS G12Y Causing a False-Positive KRAS G12C Result With an Indistinguishable PCR Pattern in Lung Adenocarcinoma.
records.abstract: KRAS G12C is an actionable alteration in non-small cell lung cancer, making accurate molecular identification essential for treatment selection. A 61-year-old man with metastatic lung adenocarcinoma showed a KRAS G12C-positive reaction on the AmoyDx Pan Lung Cancer PCR Panel (AmoyDx PLC panel). After progression on first-line chemoimmunotherapy, sotorasib was administered, but progressive disease was observed at the first radiologic assessment. Subsequent NGS-based comprehensive genomic profiling of the same pretreatment FFPE block identified KRAS G12Y (c.34_35delinsTA; variant allele frequency, 25.8%), with no sequence reads supporting KRAS G12C. This prompted suspicion of a false-positive PCR result. Repeat AmoyDx PLC panel testing reproduced the G12C-positive reaction and testing of a KRAS G12Y plasmid likewise yielded a G12C-positive reaction without additional KRAS-associated signals, confirming cross-reactivity. KRAS G12Y can therefore mimic genuine KRAS G12C in mutation-specific PCR testing and may lead to inappropriate genotype-directed therapy.

records.title: DNA methylation in glioma: clinical biomarkers and emerging biosensor-based diagnostics.
records.abstract: Gliomas are the most common malignant primary tumors of the central nervous system (CNS) and are characterized by marked molecular heterogeneity, aggressive clinical behavior, and poor patient outcomes. Among the epigenetic alterations implicated in glioma pathogenesis, DNA methylation has emerged as a key regulatory mechanism with important diagnostic, prognostic, and predictive value. Clinically established biomarkers, including O6-methylguanine-DNA methyltransferase (MGMT) promoter methylation and the glioma CpG island methylator phenotype (G-CIMP), have transformed patient stratification and therapeutic decision-making, while additional methylation signatures continue to expand the molecular classification of glioma. Conventional methylation detection methods, although highly accurate, remain limited by their cost, complexity, and dependence on specialized laboratory infrastructure. This review summarizes current knowledge of DNA methylation biology in glioma, discusses established and emerging methylation biomarkers, and critically examines recent advances in biosensor-based detection technologies, including electrochemical, optical, microfluidic, and nanopore-based platforms, together with enzyme-assisted and immunoaffinity-based molecular recognition strategies that can be combined with these transducers. These technologies, particularly when combined with nanomaterials, signal amplification strategies, and liquid biopsy approaches, offer highly sensitive, rapid, and minimally invasive detection of methylated circulating tumor DNA, supporting the development of point-of-care diagnostics. Despite encouraging progress, challenges related to analytical standardization, tumor heterogeneity, cross-reactivity, large-scale clinical validation, and regulatory translation remain significant barriers to routine implementation. By integrating recent advances in glioma epigenetics with emerging biosensing technologies, this review provides a comprehensive overview of the current landscape and highlights future opportunities for translating DNA methylation biomarkers into clinically accessible precision diagnostic platforms.
